questions.question_text: How many definitions of 'software architecture' exist?
questions.explanation: There is no single definition; various authors and standards (e.g., IEEE, SEI) provide different definitions [2].

options.text: Exactly one for all kinds of systems.
One for every kind of software system (e.g. 'embedded', 'real-time', 'decision support', 'web', 'batch'...).
A dozen or more different definitions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following aspects are covered by the term 'software architecture'?
questions.explanation: Software architecture includes components (building blocks), cross-cutting concepts, and interfaces. Coding conventions and hardware sizing are typically implementation or infrastructure details [2, 3].

options.text: Components
Cross-cutting concepts
(internal and external) Interfaces
Coding conventions
Hardware sizing

questions.question_text: Which FOUR of the following statements about (crosscutting) concepts are most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Concepts increase consistency, can define constraints, can be implemented by single blocks, and help achieve uniform handling (e.g., exceptions) [3, 4].

options.text: Uniform usage of concepts reduces coupling between building blocks.
The definition of appropriate concepts ensures the pattern compliance of the architecture.
Uniform exception handling can be achieved when architects agree with developers upon a suitable concept prior to implementation.
For each quality goal there should be an explicitly documented concept.
Concepts are a means to increase consistency.
A concept can define constraints for the implementation of many building blocks.
A concept might be implemented by a single building block.

questions.question_text: In your project, three architects and seven developers are working on the documentation of the software architecture. Which methods are appropriate in order to achieve a consistent and adequate documentation, and which are not?
questions.explanation: Central coordination and templates ensure consistency. Automatic extraction is often insufficient for architectural concepts [4].

rows.text: The lead architect coordinates the creation of the documentation.
Identical templates are used for the documentation.
All parts of the documentation are automatically extracted from the source code.

questions.question_text: Which of the following techniques are best suited to illustrate the workflow or behavior of the system at runtime?
questions.explanation: Flowcharts, Activity Diagrams, Sequence Diagrams, and numbered lists describe dynamic behavior. Class diagrams and interface tables describe static structure [5, 6].

options.text: Flowcharts
Activity Diagrams
Depiction of screen flows (sequence of user interactions)
Sequence diagram
Linear Venn diagram
Numbered list of sequential steps
Tabular description of interfaces
Class diagrams

questions.question_text: Which of the following principles apply to testing?
questions.explanation: Testing cannot prove the absence of errors, only their presence. Errors often cluster in specific components [6].

options.text: In general, it is not possible to discover all errors in the system.
In components with many known previous errors, the chances for additional errors are high.
Sufficient testing can show that a program is free of errors.
Testing shows the existence of errors rather than the absence of errors.
Functional programming does not allow automated testing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the information hiding principle are true and which are false?
questions.explanation: Information hiding (encapsulation) increases flexibility by hiding implementation details from callers. It does not hinder bottom-up work [7].

rows.text: Adhering to the information hiding principle increases flexibility for modifications.
Information hiding involves deliberately hiding information from callers or consumers of the building block.
Information hiding makes it harder to work bottom-up.
Information hiding is a derivative of the approach of incremental refinement along the control flow.

questions.question_text: What are the most important goals of software architecture?
questions.explanation: The primary goals are achieving quality requirements and enabling understanding among stakeholders [8].

options.text: Improve accuracy of patterns in structure and implementation.
Achieve quality requirements in a comprehensible way.
Enable cost-effective integration and acceptance tests of the system.
Enable a basic understanding of structures and concepts for the development team and other stakeholders.

questions.question_text: Put yourself in the position of a software architect for a large, distributed business application. Which of the following statements is true and which is false?
questions.explanation: Architects design for change based on stakeholder input and drive decisions via quality requirements. Architecture is rarely independent of infrastructure in large systems [9].

rows.text: The architect collaborates with the stakeholders to determine where the requirements will change often, and designs the architecture such that changes can occur without requiring extensive restructuring.
Required product qualities should drive your architectural decisions.
The software architecture can be designed completely independent of the hardware and infrastructure.

questions.question_text: What are your most important responsibilities as a software architect with respect to requirements?
questions.explanation: Architects support clarifying quality requirements, check technical feasibility, and identify business opportunities through technology [10].

options.text: Support the business people to specify explicit and concrete quality requirements.
Help to identify new business opportunities based on your technology know-how.
Reject business requirements that contain technical risks.
Capture all business requirements in a terminology that can be understood by your development team.
Check requirements for technological feasibility.

questions.question_text: You are responsible as an architect for keeping a legacy system up and running. What are the most important action items on your agenda?
questions.explanation: Key maintenance tasks include updating documentation, analyzing impact of new requirements, and suggesting technology updates [11].

options.text: Negotiating the maintenance budget for your team.
Assuring up-to-date documentation of the deployed system.
Analyzing the impact of new requirements on the current system.
Encouraging the teammembers to learn new programming languages.
Suggesting technology updates in addition to the business requirements to your management.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding architecture decisions are true, which are false?
questions.explanation: ADRs help context understanding. Decisions should be changeable if needed. Quality requirements drive decisions [12].

rows.text: Architecture decisions never need to be written down because they are already known to the development team.
An architecture decision record helps to make the decision’s context understood.
Once a decision has been made on a central or fundamental framework (e.g. persistence framework), that decision must not be changed.
Quality requirements help significantly with architecture decisions.

questions.question_text: Decide for each of the following statements about agile development whether it is true or false.
questions.explanation: Agile iterations can impact architecture. Agile does not necessarily mean higher effort or zero documentation [13].

rows.text: Each iteration of an agile development approach could have an impact on the fundamental architecture decisions.
The total effort spent on architectural work is much higher in iterative projects compared to waterfall projects.
Agile projects do not need architecture documents since the development team uses daily standup-meetings to communicate decisions.
If your systems consist of a set of microservices there is no need for a central architecture document.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding project goals and architectural goals is true and which is false.
questions.explanation: Project goals include both functional/quality reqs. Architectural goals are derived from quality reqs. Stakeholders care about both [14].

rows.text: Project Goals can include functional requirements as well as quality requirements.
Architectural goals are derived from the quality requirements for the system or product.
Business stakeholders should concentrate on business goals and not interfere with architectural goals.
To avoid conflicts, business goals and architectural goals should be non-overlapping sets.

questions.question_text: What does the rule 'explicit, not implicit' mean for architecture work? Choose the best-fitting answers.
questions.explanation: Assumptions and prerequisites for decisions must be made explicit to avoid misunderstandings [15].

options.text: Architects should avoid recursive structures and replace them by explicit loops.
Architects should make the assumptions leading to decisions explicit.
Architects should explicitly insist on natural language explanations for each building block.
Architects should explicitly insist on written or at least verbal justifications for development effort estimates.
Architects should make prerequisites for their decisions explicit.

questions.question_text: There are many approaches that lead to a software architecture. Which of the following are the most often found in practice?
questions.explanation: Domain Driven Design, View-based development, and Bottom-up design are common practical approaches [16].

options.text: User interface driven design
Domain driven design
View based architecture development
Bottom-up design
Majority voting

questions.question_text: Several architecture development methods suggest a view-based approach. Which of the following views are most often used?
questions.explanation: Context view, Building Block view, and Runtime view are standard architectural views [16].

options.text: Physical database view
Context view
Building Block/Component view
Test-driven view
Configuration view
Runtime view

questions.question_text: When documenting a building block of your software architecture, what information should the black-box description contain?
questions.explanation: Black-box descriptions must focus on public interfaces and responsibilities, hiding internals [17].

options.text: Public interfaces.
Responsibility of the building block.
Internal structure of the building block.
Specification of the implementation details.

questions.question_text: Which prerequisites have to be fulfilled before developing a software architecture? Pick the most appropriate answers.
questions.explanation: Knowing the important qualities and organizational constraints is essential. Requirements don't need to be 100% complete/detailed upfront [18].

options.text: The requirements specification for the system is complete, detailed and consistent.
The most important qualities for the system are known.
Organizational constraints are known.
The programming language has been selected.
Hardware for the development team is available.

questions.question_text: Which factors can influence the design of a software architecture? Pick the most appropriate answers.
questions.explanation: Architecture is influenced by technical, organizational, and political factors (like internal power structures or vendor relationships). 'Virtual' is not a standard category of influencing factors in this context.

options.text: Political.
Organizational.
Technical.
Virtual.

questions.question_text: Which of the following qualities can most likely be improved by using a layered architecture?
questions.explanation: Layered architectures primarily improve maintainability and flexibility/modifiability by separating concerns. They often incur a slight performance penalty due to overhead.

options.text: Runtime efficiency (performance).
Flexibility in modifying or changing the system.
Flexibility at runtime (configurability).
Non-repudiability.

questions.question_text: Which type of problems provide a good fit for the Pipes & Filter Pattern?
questions.explanation: Pipes & Filters is ideal for processing data streams and decoupling steps in a processing chain. It is generally not suited for managing global state.

options.text: Management of global application state
IT systems which process data streams
Decoupling multiple steps of an execution
Temporal decoupling of an application

questions.question_text: Which goals are you trying to achieve with the dependency inversion principle?
questions.explanation: Dependency Inversion aims to decouple high-level modules from low-level modules by having both depend on abstractions (interfaces).

options.text: Big building blocks shall not depend on small building blocks.
Components shall be able to create dependent components more easily.
Building blocks shall only depend on each other via abstractions.

questions.question_text: What are characteristics of tight (high) or loose (low) coupling?
questions.explanation: Direct calls without interfaces and shared data/tables create tight coupling. Using Dependency Inversion fosters loose coupling.

rows.text: Building blocks directly call dependent building blocks, i.e., without using indirect calls via interfaces or abstractions.
Building blocks use shared complex data structures.
Building blocks use a shared table (for read- and write operations) within a relational database.
When designing building blocks, you have consistently applied the dependency inversion principle.

questions.question_text: Which statements about the principle 'Don’t repeat yourself' (DRY) fit best? In other words: What could happen, if parts of the source code or configuration do exist in multiple copies in the system?
questions.explanation: DRY aims to reduce redundancy. Strict adherence can sometimes increase coupling (as things are unified). If code is redundant, those parts can be changed independently (which is a risk if they *should* stay in sync, but a property of redundancy).

options.text: DRY reduces security.
Strict adherence to DRY could lead to higher coupling.
The components of the system that contain redundant code can be improved independently of each other.
Adherence to DRY leads to additional attack vectors in IT security.
Applying the Layer patterns allows a consistent application of the DRY principle.

questions.question_text: You can communicate aspects of your software architecture verbally and/or in writing. How do these variants correlate? Decide for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.
questions.explanation: Verbal communication is good for immediate feedback and explanation, supplementing written docs. Feedback doesn't *always* need to be written (though often helpful). Writing doesn't *always* have to precede verbal communication.

rows.text: Verbal communication should supplement written documentation.
Feedback to architecture decisions should always be done in writing to ensure traceability.
Written documentation should always precede verbal communication.
Architects should pick one variant (verbal or written) and stick to this choice during the whole development.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about notations for architectural views is true and which is false?
questions.explanation: BPMN can be used for architecture (processes). UML Deployment diagrams are standard but not the *only* way (e.g., simple boxes/lines or text). Package diagrams are valid for building blocks. Informal notations are fine if a legend explains them.

rows.text: Business Process Model & Notation (BPMN) should only be used by Business Analysts and not for architecture documentation.
UML deployment models are the only way to document the mapping of software components to infrastructure.
UML Package Diagrams can be used to capture the building-block view of software architectures.
As long as the notation is explained (e.g. by a legend), any notation can be sufficient to describe building block structures and collaboration.

questions.question_text: Which architectural views have the most practical application for developing software architectures?
questions.explanation: The Building Block (Component) View and Deployment View are fundamental for development. 'Pattern View' and 'Observer View' are not standard architectural views.

options.text: Pattern View.
Observer View.
Building-Block View (Component View).
Deployment View.

questions.question_text: The context view might contain a business context and a technical context, or both. Pick the most appropriate answers that apply to the technical context.
questions.explanation: The technical context focuses on physical channels (hardware, protocols) and technical interfaces. It is distinct from the business context (domain entities, stakeholders). Pricing is usually a management concern, not context view.

options.text: The technical context contains the physical channels between your system and its environment.
The technical context contains all the infrastructure on which the components of your system are deployed.
The technical context should include hardware pricing or pricing of cloud services used as infrastructure for your architecture.
The technical context contains information about the chosen programming language as well as all frameworks used to implement your software architecture.
The technical context might contain different elements than the business context.

questions.question_text: Software architecture documentation could contain descriptions of cross-cutting concerns. Pick the best reasons why documentation of cross-cutting concerns is useful.
questions.explanation: Documenting cross-cutting concerns prevents redundancy (don't describe the same error handling in every module) and supports reuse across products.

options.text: Cross-cutting concepts should focus on the domain and be free of technical information.
Aspects or concepts that are used in multiple parts of your software architecture should be described in a non-redundant way.
Cross-cutting concepts can be reused in more products within the same organization.
Cross-cutting concepts should be implemented by specialists. Therefore, separate documentation is useful.

questions.question_text: What are guidelines for good interface design? Check which of the following statements are true and which are false.
questions.explanation: Interfaces should be easy to learn and write code for. They should generally hide implementation details. They specify functional and often non-functional aspects. Local and remote calls differ significantly (latency, failure modes).

rows.text: Use of interfaces should be easy to learn.
It should be possible to write client code for the interface, that is reasonably easy to understand.
An interface should provide access to a comprehensive set of implementation details.
Interface specifications should contain functional and non-functional aspects.
Local and remote calls to an interface should behave identically in all aspects.

questions.question_text: One definition says: 'Software architecture is the sum of all the decisions you have taken during development.' Check which of the following statements about architectural/design decisions are true and which are false.
questions.explanation: Decisions impact structure and often have interdependencies. Tradeoffs (e.g., performance vs. security) should be explicit. While documenting justification is good practice, claiming architects must justify *all* decisions in writing is too absolute/burdensome.

rows.text: Architectural decisions can impact the structure of the building block or components.
Software architects shall justify all design decisions in writing.
Architectural decisions can have interdependencies between each other.
Tradeoffs between conflicting quality requirements should be explicit decisions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are typical reasons for introducing an architecture documentation and which are not typical reasons?
questions.explanation: Documentation aids onboarding, distributed work, maintenance/enhancement, and compliance. It is not primarily for supporting automated testing or just to keep developers busy.

rows.text: To support onboarding of new developers.
To support the automated testing approach of the system.
To support the work of distributed teams.
To assist in future enhancements of the product.
To conform to regulatory or legal constraints.
To ensure that developers have enough work to do.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of qualities are usually in conflict to each other, and which are not?
questions.explanation: Usability and Security often conflict (e.g., complex passwords vs. ease of use). Runtime configurability adds complexity, potentially hurting robustness. Understandability usually aids readability. Security generally supports functional correctness.

rows.text: Understandability – Readability
Usability – Security
Runtime configurability – Robustness
Security – Functional correctness

questions.question_text: ISO 25010 provides generic quality characteristics for software systems. How can quality requirements concerning these characteristics be made more concrete?
questions.explanation: Quality scenarios are the standard method for making abstract quality goals concrete and measurable.

options.text: By developing UI prototypes.
By defining explicit interfaces.
By discussing or writing quality scenarios.
By creating automated tests.

questions.question_text: Which of the following points are best suited to support the qualitative evaluation of a software architecture with regard to the fulfillment of quality requirements?
questions.explanation: Qualitative evaluation relies on expert analysis of models, dependencies, scenarios, and artifacts like log files. Team size or org structure are project management factors, not direct architecture evaluation artifacts.

options.text: Quantitative dependency analysis.
Architecture models.
Quality scenarios.
Team size.
Log files.
Organizational structure.

questions.question_text: You try to analyze your architecture quantitatively. Which are the most appropriate indicators for architectural problem areas?
questions.explanation: High coupling and error clusters are strong quantitative indicators of architectural issues. Naming/comments are code quality. Test case count is a testing metric.

options.text: High coupling of components.
Names of public methods do not reflect their purpose.
Missing comments.
Clusters of errors in certain building blocks of the system.
Number of test cases per component.

questions.question_text: You try to quantitatively analyze your architecture. Which three of the following properties can you measure reliably in your software architecture? Pick the best fitting answers.
questions.explanation: You can reliably measure LOC (size), change rate (via VCS), and number of contributors. Cohesion and security level are difficult to measure as a single reliable quantitative number.

options.text: Size of building blocks (e.g. LOC).
Change rate of the source code of components.
Cohesion of the architectural components.
Security level of a component.
Number of the developers that contributed to a specific component.
